profiles.name: Andrea Robbins
profiles.description: Andrea Robbins is an Olympia anti-war organizer who also worked with the Olympia-Rafah Solidarity Mural Project. On November 13, 2007, she joined a women’s blockade at the Port of Olympia, sitting in front of the main gate to stop a Stryker convoy. Police ordered the group to disperse and arrested her when she remained. The arrested women were held for about seven hours and released early on November 14. The surveillance and police response later became part of Panagacos v. Towery, a civil suit over Army infiltration of Port Militarization Resistance and the sharing of intelligence with local police.
profiles.finding: Vimeo interview explicitly identifies Olympia-Rafah mural coordinator Andrea Robbins; video still extraction/rights unresolved. Artist Andrea Robbins not linked. Profile describes seven-hour custody, flagged for separate eligibility review.

profiles.name: Brendan Maslauskas Dunn
profiles.description: Brendan Maslauskas Dunn is an anti-war organizer, journalist and member of the Industrial Workers of the World who helped found the Evergreen State College chapter of Students for a Democratic Society and organized with Port Militarization Resistance. Police arrested him for pedestrian interference on May 22, 2006 after he stood in front of a Stryker convoy approaching the Port of Olympia. Seattle police arrested him again at an anti-war rally in Cal Anderson Park on October 5, 2006 after an officer seized an anarcho-syndicalist flag carried by his group; the charges were later dismissed and the arrest led to civil litigation. A federal decision also references a June 2007 Tacoma arrest, but the accessible record does not establish its exact day or a custody interval. He later helped expose Army employee John Towery’s infiltration of the anti-war movement.
profiles.finding: Democracy Now and IWW Flag3 caption corroborate activist; Shadowproof author avatar downloaded and visually confirmed generic silhouette, rejected. IWW group portrait remains crop/credit lead.

profiles.name: Chris Grande
profiles.description: Chris Grande was a Port Militarization Resistance activist and plaintiff in Panagacos v. Towery, the federal civil-rights suit challenging Army infiltration of the Olympia anti-war movement. Court records document that police exposed him to pepper spray or pepper balls during Port of Olympia protests on November 7, 10 and 13, 2007. Those records do not document an arrest, booking, criminal charge or jail confinement for Grande in those incidents.
profiles.finding: Evergreen newspaper and Olympia Food Co-op identify local organizer; Photomatica staff portrait not independently linked. Profile itself lacks custody evidence; flagged without alteration.

profiles.name: Jeffrey Berryhill
profiles.description: Jeffrey “Jeff” Berryhill was a Port Militarization Resistance and Students for a Democratic Society organizer. Tacoma police arrested him in the predawn hours of March 5, 2007 during protests against military shipments at the Port of Tacoma, after an officer shot him in the thigh at close range with a rubber projectile. He was charged with resisting arrest and assaulting police, supporters posted bond, and the charges were later dismissed after video contradicted the police account. Olympia police detained and arrested him again on July 27, 2007. The sources establish both arrests but do not provide exact release dates. Berryhill later joined Panagacos v. Towery, the civil suit concerning Army infiltration and police surveillance of the movement.
profiles.finding: Fermilab and Bethel faculty portraits are not linked to PMR activist and rejected. IWW byline/photo credits not subject identification.

profiles.description: Nancy Conde Rubio, age 37, a high-ranking FARC member who oversaw the FARCs logistics and communications network used to transport three American hostages in 2003. Extradited to the U.S.; convicted of conspiracy and material-support charges; 138 months federal prison + 36 months supervised release.

profiles.name: Sabri Benkahla
profiles.description:
Connected to the Virginia jihad network, a group of men who played paintball as a means to train for combat under the guidance of controversial imam Ali al-Timimi, Sabri Benkahla lied to authorities about training with militants in Pakistan, made other false statements, and obstructed justice in the Virginia jihad trial. Benkahla was acquitted at trial of fighting for the Taliban, and after his acquittal, federal prosecutors filed perjury charges, for which he was convicted.

Case characteristics: FBI confidential informant, FISA surveillance. Organization referenced in charging documents: Taliban.

Case data and description from The Intercept's Trial and Terror project (Trevor Aaronson and Margot Williams), licensed CC BY-NC. Source: https://github.com/theintercept/trial-and-terror-data
profiles.finding: Some Noise episode and court opinion corroborate identity; no usable portrait verified.

profiles.name: Philip Chinn
profiles.description: Evergreen State College student and PMR organizer in Olympia. Arrested multiple times during the 2006-2008 PMR campaign. The defining incident: on May 30, 2007 the Washington State Patrol pulled Chinn over near the Port of Aberdeen, falsely arrested him for DUI, and held him 36 hours despite a blood-alcohol level of 0.000. He sued the WSP under 42 U.S.C. §1983; the State of Washington settled for in excess of $400,000 — one of the largest false-arrest settlements ever obtained by a Washington anti-war organizer. Chinn was not a named plaintiff in Panagacos v. Towery but was likewise a target of John Towery's surveillance operation.
profiles.finding: Seattle Weekly settlement story is promising lead; older Chicago obituary portrait and Texas genealogy namesakes rejected.

profiles.name: Mohamed Shorbagi
profiles.description:
Mohamed Shorbagi, a Georgia imam, was connected to the Holy Land Foundation and charged with providing material support to Hamas. In pleading guilty, Shorbagi agreed to cooperate with the government and testified in the trial of Abdelhaleem Ashqar and Muhammad Salah.

Case characteristics: cooperated with prosecutors. Organization referenced in charging documents: Hamas.

Case data and description from The Intercept's Trial and Terror project (Trevor Aaronson and Margot Williams), licensed CC BY-NC. Source: https://github.com/theintercept/trial-and-terror-data

profiles.name: Melanie McPherson
profiles.description: Melanie McPherson was an Army reservist trained as a photojournalist who left her unit before Middle East deployment. She feared assignment to Iraq in a different role. A February 2007 court-martial convicted her of desertion and imposed three months' confinement, demotion, and a bad-conduct discharge.
profiles.finding: Courage to Resist directly identifies subject thumbnail at /images/stories/profiles/mcphearson-100.jpg. 100x100 source too small for preferred profile treatment; larger original remains a lead.
